record.original_question: For a given $A ^n x n$, let $ V$ denote an approximate invariant subspace of dimension $d$ of $A$, in the sense that there exists some $d$-dimensional invariant subspace $ V$ of $A$ such that $ ( V, V)$ is small. Let $ W$ be some other subspace of dimension $r<n-d$. Suppose the columns of $Q$ form an orthonormal basis for the (generically) $d+r$ dimensional space $ Q = V + W$. Provide conditions that will ensure that $d$ eigenvalues of $Q*AQ$ approximate the $d$ eigenvalues of $A$ associated with the invariant subspace $ V$. Impose assumptions about the eigenvalues of $A$ corresponding to $ V$, as needed.

evidence.quote: For a given $A\in\C^{n\times n}$, let $\widehat{\cal V}$ denote an approximate invariant subspace of dimension $d$ of $A$, in the sense that there exists some $d$-dimensional invariant subspace ${\cal V}$ of $A$ such that $\angle({\cal V},\widehat{\cal V})$ is small. Let ${\cal W}$ be some other subspace of dimension $r<n-d$. Suppose the columns of $Q$ form an orthonormal basis for the (generically) $d+r$ dimensional space ${\cal Q} = \widehat{\cal V} + {\cal W}$. % Provide conditions that will ensure that $d$ eigenvalues of $Q^*AQ$ approximate the $d$ eigenvalues of $A$ associated with the invariant subspace ${\cal V}$. Impose assumptions about the eigenvalues of $A$ corresponding to $\cal V$, as needed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$, and let $\mathcal{V}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ be a $d$-dimensional invariant subspace of $A$, so that $A\mathcal{V}\subseteq\mathcal{V}$. Let $\widehat{\mathcal{V}}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ be another $d$-dimensional subspace which is an approximate invariant subspace, in the sense that the largest principal angle $\angle(\mathcal{V},\widehat{\mathcal{V}})$ is small. Let $\mathcal{W}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ be a further subspace of dimension $r$ with $r < n-d$, and assume that, generically, $\dim(\widehat{\mathcal{V}}+\mathcal{W})=d+r$. Set $\mathcal{Q}=\widehat{\mathcal{V}}+\mathcal{W}$ and let $Q\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times(d+r)}$ have orthonormal columns spanning $\mathcal{Q}$, so the Rayleigh–Ritz matrix is $H = Q^*AQ\in\mathbb{C}^{(d+r)\times(d+r)}$.
 
Denote by $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ the eigenvalues of $A$ associated with $\mathcal{V}$ (i.e.\ the eigenvalues of $A\big|_{\mathcal{V}}$), and by $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_{d+r}$ the eigenvalues of $H$ (the Ritz values of $A$ from $\mathcal{Q}$).
 
Problem. Formulate and prove explicit conditions — including any necessary spectral separation hypotheses on $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ relative to the remaining eigenvalues of $A$, and on the geometric configuration of $\widehat{\mathcal{V}}$, $\mathcal{W}$, and the invariant subspaces of $A$ — under which exactly $d$ of the Ritz values $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_{d+r}$ approximate $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$, and provide quantitative bounds on the corresponding errors $|\mu_{i_k}-\lambda_k|$ in terms of $\angle(\mathcal{V},\widehat{\mathcal{V}})$, the spectral gaps, and $\|A\|$.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this exact open problem could be confirmed. Classical Rayleigh–Ritz / Ritz value perturbation theory (Saad, Stewart–Sun, Knyazev, Jia, and others) provides bounds when the trial subspace itself is close to an invariant subspace, but the refined setting where the trial subspace is an enlargement $\widehat{\mathcal{V}}+\mathcal{W}$ with only $\widehat{\mathcal{V}}$ approximating an invariant subspace appears not to have a definitive published answer of the form requested.

status_evidence.title: Ritz values and Rayleigh–Ritz procedure (general references)
status_evidence.snippet: The problem is posed as an open question regarding conditions ensuring d Ritz values of Q*AQ approximate the eigenvalues of A associated with an invariant subspace.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open research question without a complete published solution at the time of posing.
